福爾摩沙小導遊臺南 Tainan・安平區

安平樹屋Anping Tree House

容我介紹一棟有兩位主人的建築：房子是人蓋的，但被榕樹接管了。這裡原本是德記洋行後方的倉庫，建於十九世紀末。後來成為日本鹽業會社的倉庫，並擴建到今天的規模。二戰後歸台灣製鹽總廠使用；鹽廠遷走後，倉庫就被遺忘了。接著，大自然搬了進來。榕樹的根爬滿每一面牆，樹冠變成了屋頂。榕樹的氣生根能直接吸收潮濕空氣中的水分。根部會分泌溶解石灰岩的酸。舊灰漿裡的牡蠣殼是碳酸鈣，跟石灰岩一樣。對榕樹來說，這些牆不是障礙，是養分。如今，木棧道、鋼構步道與觀景平台讓我們爬上樹冠。松鼠和鳥兒把這裡當成遊樂場。請大家走在步道上。

May I present a building with two owners: humans built it, but the banyan trees took it over. This was a warehouse behind the Tait and Company Merchant House, built around the end of the nineteenth century. Later the Japan Salt Corporation used it and extended it to its present size. After World War Two, it passed to the Taiwan Salt Corporation. When the salt company moved away, the warehouse was abandoned. Then nature moved in. Banyan roots crept over every wall, and the canopy became the roof. Their aerial roots drink moisture straight from the humid air. Their roots make an acid that dissolves limestone. Oyster shell in the old mortar is calcium carbonate, the same as limestone. To a banyan tree, these walls were not an obstacle. They were food. Today, wooden and steel walkways and viewing platforms let you climb to the treetops. Squirrels and birds treat this place as their playground. Please stay on the walkways.

One-minute intro

為什麼值得來

Why it matters & history

安平樹屋原是德記洋行的倉庫，荒廢後被榕樹的根和枝幹整個包覆，形成建築與老樹共生的奇特景觀，是臺灣最常被拍照的老倉庫之一。

The Anping Tree House was a warehouse of Tait and Company. After it was abandoned, banyan roots and branches wrapped the whole building, so trees and walls now hold each other up.

  1. 清末 Late Qing德記洋行在商館後方設倉庫，存放出口貨物。Tait and Company builds a warehouse behind its office to store export goods.
  2. 日治時期 Japanese era日本鹽業會社使用並擴建。A Japanese salt company takes it over and enlarges it.
  3. 戰後 After 1945臺灣製鹽總廠使用，遷走後倉庫荒廢，榕樹長滿屋頂和牆。The salt works uses it; after they leave, banyans take over the roof and walls.
  4. 2004整理後以「安平樹屋」對外開放。It opens to the public as the Anping Tree House.

認識景點

About the place

榕樹：有很多根的大樹，出名的「地盤擴張高手」。 氣生根：懸在空中的根，能直接吸收空氣中的水分。 倉庫：存放貨物的建築；這裡曾是鹽業公司的倉庫。 共生：一起生活；在這裡，建築和樹互相支撐。

banyan tree: A big tree with many roots. Banyans are famous for taking over walls and rocks. aerial roots: Roots that hang in the air. They drink moisture straight from the humid air. warehouse: A building for storing goods. This one belonged to the salt companies. symbiosis: Living together. Here, the building and the trees hold each other up.

樹冠：樹木頂端的枝葉；這裡的樹冠變成了屋頂。 棲息地：動植物的家；松鼠和鳥住在這裡。 步道、棧道：走路的通道；這裡有木棧道和鋼構步道。 觀景平台：高處的平台，可以從上方俯瞰根之屋頂。

canopy: The leafy top of the trees. Here the canopy became the roof. habitat: The home of animals and plants. Squirrels and birds live here. walkway: A path for walking, here made of wood and steel above the trees. viewing platform: A high place to look down. You can see the roof of roots from above.

石灰岩：一種岩石；榕樹的根會分泌酸來溶解它。 碳酸鈣：牡蠣殼和石灰岩的成分，舊牆的灰漿裡就有。 光斑：在比較暗的房間裡靜靜站一分鐘：光線穿過樹冠，灑成會移動的光斑。 水分、濕氣：空氣中的小水滴；安平的空氣溫暖潮濕。

limestone: A kind of rock. Banyan roots make an acid that dissolves it. calcium carbonate: What oyster shells and limestone are made of. It was in the old wall mortar. light spots: In the darker rooms, stand still for a minute: light falls through the leaf canopy in moving spots. moisture: Tiny bits of water in the air. Anping's air is warm and humid.

荒廢的、被遺棄的：沒人使用、被丟下；然後大自然就搬進來了。 洋行：外國貿易公司做生意的地方；德記洋行的白色洋樓就在樹屋旁邊。

abandoned: Left alone with no one using it. Then nature moved in. merchant house: A foreign trading company's office. Tait and Company's white merchant house stands next to the Tree House.

實景照片

Photos on site

英商德記洋行 Tait & Co. Merchant House

這棟白色兩層洋樓，是十九世紀後期英國商行德記洋行的房子。屋頂上的金色公雞風向標，告訴大家風從哪裡吹來。洋樓就在安平樹屋旁邊，今天裡面是介紹安平貿易歷史的展覽。

This white two-storey house belonged to Tait and Company, a British trading firm, in the late 1800s. A golden rooster weathervane on the roof shows which way the wind blows. The house stands right next to the Anping Tree House, and today it holds an exhibition about Anping's trading days.

根包住了牆 Roots over the Wall

榕樹的根整片爬滿老倉庫的牆，分不清哪裡是牆、哪裡是根。茂密的樹冠就像倉庫的屋頂。

Banyan roots cover the wall of the old warehouse. It is hard to tell where the wall ends and the roots begin. The leafy canopy has become the roof.
